lit: the language of birds and the fragrance of flowers

use.how: Predicate or attributive describing a place, usually in spring: 公园里鸟语花香 / 一个鸟语花香的早晨. Said of gardens, parks and countryside.

near.diff: 春暖花开 marks the season when it turns warm and things bloom; 鸟语花香 paints a particular place full of birdsong and scent.

cue: You step into a garden on an April morning: songbirds in every tree and the scent of blossom in the air. How do you describe the place?

ctx.s: 春天的公园里{鸟语花香}，很多人来散步。
ctx.en: In spring the park is full of birdsong and flowers, and lots of people come for a walk.

ctx.s: 这个小区种了很多树，早上推开窗就是一片{鸟语花香}。
ctx.en: This estate has planted lots of trees; open the window in the morning and it's all birdsong and blossom.

ctx.s: “你老家怎么样？”“院子里种满了花，树上整天有鸟叫，真是{鸟语花香}。”
ctx.en: "What's your hometown like?" "The yard is full of flowers and birds sing in the trees all day; it's all birdsong and blossom."

ctx.s: 她在作文里写道：清晨的校园{鸟语花香}，同学们在大声读书。
ctx.en: She wrote in her essay: in the early morning the campus is full of birdsong and flowers, and students are reading aloud.

ctx.s: 退休后他在院子里种花养鸟，家里一年到头{鸟语花香}。
ctx.en: After retiring he planted flowers and kept birds in his yard, so all year round his home is full of birdsong and blossom.

ctx.s: 这家民宿的院子里{鸟语花香}，早上是被鸟叫醒的。
ctx.en: The courtyard of this guesthouse is full of birdsong and flowers; in the morning you wake up to the birds.

bad.s: 这道菜{鸟语花香}，大家都喜欢吃。
bad.why: It describes a natural scene with birds and flowers, not the smell or taste of food.

bad.s: 他说话{鸟语花香}，大家都爱听。
bad.why: It is not about pleasant speech; niǎo yǔ is birdsong, and the phrase describes a place, never a person's way of talking.

mean: the warmth and blossom of spring
lit: spring turns warm and the flowers open

use.how: Often a time expression for when winter is over: 等到春暖花开的时候 / 春暖花开的季节; also a predicate: 北京春暖花开了.

near.diff: 鸟语花香 describes how a place looks and sounds; 春暖花开 names the time of year when it gets warm and things bloom.

cue: Your friend wants to visit now, in January. You suggest waiting until the cold is over and the trees are in blossom.

ctx.s: 等到{春暖花开}的时候，我们一起去爬山吧。
ctx.en: When spring comes and the flowers are out, let's go hiking together.

ctx.s: 三月底，北京终于{春暖花开}了。
ctx.en: By the end of March, Beijing has finally warmed up and come into bloom.

ctx.s: “什么时候去南京最好？”“{春暖花开}的四月，到处都是樱花。”
ctx.en: "When is the best time to go to Nanjing?" "April, when it's warm and blooming; there are cherry blossoms everywhere."

ctx.s: 冬天太冷，这家农场要到{春暖花开}才重新开放。
ctx.en: Winter is too cold; this farm won't reopen until spring warms up and things bloom.

ctx.s: 经过一个漫长的冬天，人们都盼着{春暖花开}。
ctx.en: After a long winter, everyone is longing for the warmth and flowers of spring.

ctx.s: 老人说，熬过这个冬天，到了{春暖花开}，身体就会好起来。
ctx.en: The old man said that once he got through this winter, when spring came, his health would pick up.

bad.s: 十月的北京{春暖花开}，最适合旅游。
bad.en: (meant: Beijing in October has lovely weather)
bad.why: It refers only to spring. For pleasant autumn weather the idiom is qiū gāo qì shuǎng.

bad.s: 他升职以后，心情{春暖花开}。
bad.en: (meant: after his promotion he was in a great mood)
bad.why: It describes the season, not a person's mood. For great joy say xīn huā nù fàng, or simply that he is very happy.

lit: in autumn the sky is high and the air is crisp

use.how: Predicate or attributive about autumn weather only: 十月秋高气爽 / 秋高气爽的日子. Often used when recommending outings.

near.diff: 风和日丽 is a calm sunny day in any mild season; 秋高气爽 is specifically the clear, cool, dry feel of autumn.

cue: It's late September: the summer humidity has gone, the sky looks high and blue, and the air feels cool and clean.

ctx.s: 十月的北京{秋高气爽}，是旅游的好季节。
ctx.en: In October Beijing has clear, crisp autumn weather; it's a great season to visit.

ctx.s: 国庆节前后{秋高气爽}，很多人去郊外爬山。
ctx.en: Around National Day in early October the autumn air is clear and crisp, and lots of people go hiking outside the city.

ctx.s: “这几天天气怎么样？”“{秋高气爽}，不冷不热，特别舒服。”
ctx.en: "How's the weather these days?" "Clear and crisp, not cold, not hot; really comfortable."

ctx.s: 运动会选在九月底举行，正赶上{秋高气爽}。
ctx.en: The sports day was held at the end of September, just in time for the clear autumn weather.

ctx.s: 夏天闷热了好几个月，现在终于{秋高气爽}了。
ctx.en: After months of muggy summer, it's finally cool and clear autumn weather.

ctx.s: 夏天的潮气终于散了，趁着{秋高气爽}，把被子拿出去晒晒吧。
ctx.en: The summer damp has finally gone; let's take the quilts out to air while the autumn weather is dry and clear.

bad.s: 四月{秋高气爽}，花都开了。
bad.en: (meant: April has lovely weather and the flowers are out)
bad.why: It is only said of autumn. For warm, blooming spring weather use chūn nuǎn huā kāi.

bad.s: 他这个人{秋高气爽}，从来不生气。
bad.why: It describes weather, not personality; shuǎng here is crisp air. For an easygoing person say kāi lǎng or shuǎng kuai.

mean: a frozen world of ice and snow
lit: ice in the sky, snow on the ground

use.how: Describes a deeply frozen landscape or winter, often 在冰天雪地里 or as a predicate: 东北的冬天冰天雪地. Often stresses hardship.

cue: Your friend in the far north sends a photo in January: frozen rivers, snow piled high everywhere, thirty below outside.

ctx.s: 东北的冬天{冰天雪地}，外面经常零下二十多度。
ctx.en: Winters in the Northeast are a world of ice and snow; it's often more than twenty below outside.

ctx.s: 孩子们在{冰天雪地}里堆雪人，玩得很开心。
ctx.en: The children were building snowmen out in the ice and snow, having a great time.

ctx.s: “你在哈尔滨冷不冷？”“外面{冰天雪地}，可屋里有暖气，一点儿也不冷。”
ctx.en: "Are you cold in Harbin?" "Outside it's all ice and snow, but there's heating indoors, so I'm not cold at all."

ctx.s: 快递员在{冰天雪地}中送货，真不容易。
ctx.en: Couriers delivering parcels through the ice and snow have a really hard time.

ctx.s: 登山队被困在{冰天雪地}的山顶上，等了两天才获救。
ctx.en: The climbing team was trapped on the frozen, snowbound summit and waited two days to be rescued.

ctx.s: 他从海南来，第一次见到这样{冰天雪地}的景象，兴奋得大叫。
ctx.en: He's from Hainan, and seeing a frozen, snow-covered landscape like this for the first time, he shouted with excitement.

bad.s: 今天有点凉，外面{冰天雪地}，多穿件外套吧。
bad.why: It means everything is frozen and covered in snow; far too strong for merely cool weather.

bad.s: 她对我{冰天雪地}，一句话也不说。
bad.why: It is not used for a cold attitude toward someone; for that say lěng bīng bīng or lěng dàn.

lit: the wind is gentle and the sun is beautiful

use.how: Predicate or attributive about the weather on a given day: 那天风和日丽 / 一个风和日丽的下午. Often sets the scene for an outing or event.

near.diff: 秋高气爽 is the crisp, dry feel of autumn; 风和日丽 is any calm, sunny, mild day, most often in spring.

cue: The sun is out, there's only a light breeze, not a cloud in sight: perfect for the picnic you planned for today.

ctx.s: 春天到了，今天又{风和日丽}，我们去公园放风筝吧。
ctx.en: Spring is here and today is sunny with a gentle breeze; let's go and fly kites in the park.

ctx.s: 婚礼那天{风和日丽}，所有照片都拍得很好看。
ctx.en: The wedding day was sunny and calm, and all the photos came out beautifully.

ctx.s: “明天天气怎么样？”“预报说{风和日丽}，适合出门。”
ctx.en: "What's the weather tomorrow?" "The forecast says sunny and mild, good for going out."

ctx.s: 一个{风和日丽}的下午，他们在湖上划船。
ctx.en: One sunny, breezy afternoon, they went rowing on the lake.

ctx.s: 刚才还{风和日丽}的海面，突然刮起了大风。
ctx.en: The sea, calm and sunny a moment ago, was suddenly hit by a strong wind.

ctx.s: 老人们喜欢趁{风和日丽}的时候出来晒太阳。
ctx.en: The old folks like to come out and sit in the sun when the weather is mild and sunny.

bad.s: 外面{风和日丽}，下着小雨。
bad.en: (meant: the weather is mild, with light rain)
bad.why: It means sunny and calm; it cannot describe a rainy day.

bad.s: 他们俩的关系一直{风和日丽}。
bad.en: (meant: their relationship has always been smooth)
bad.why: It describes weather only; for a harmonious relationship say hé mù, or simply that they get on well.

lit: neither wind nor rain can stop it

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (风雨无阻地) about a routine or commitment that goes on whatever the weather: 他每天跑步，风雨无阻. Also used on notices.

cue: For twenty years the old man has walked his dog at six every morning, through storms and snow, never missing a day.

ctx.s: 爷爷每天早上去公园锻炼，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: Grandpa goes to the park to exercise every morning, rain or shine.

ctx.s: 这位快递员十年来{风雨无阻}，从没耽误过一次送货。
ctx.en: For ten years this courier has worked in all weathers and never once delayed a delivery.

ctx.s: “下这么大的雨，你还去跑步？”“说好了{风雨无阻}，当然去。”
ctx.en: "You're still going running in rain like this?" "We agreed rain or shine, so of course I'm going."

ctx.s: 她{风雨无阻}地接送孩子上学，从来没迟到过。
ctx.en: She takes her child to and from school in all weathers and has never once been late.

ctx.s: 这个早市每天清晨开门，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: This morning market opens at dawn every day, whatever the weather.

ctx.s: 活动通知上写着：比赛照常进行，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: The event notice said: the race will go ahead as planned, rain or shine.

bad.s: 今天{风雨无阻}，我们去爬山吧。
bad.why: It does not describe the weather; it says someone keeps going in spite of bad weather.

bad.s: 他做事{风雨无阻}，谁的话都不听。
bad.why: It praises dependable persistence through bad weather, not stubbornness toward people.

lit: the hills are green and the waters are lovely

use.how: Predicate or attributive praising the natural scenery of a region: 这里山清水秀 / 山清水秀的小镇.

near.diff: 鸟语花香 is the sound and scent of a garden in spring; 山清水秀 is the landscape of hills and rivers, in any season.

cue: You're describing a village in the south: green hills rise all around it and a clear river winds past the houses.

ctx.s: 桂林{山清水秀}，每年吸引很多游客。
ctx.en: Guilin has beautiful green hills and clear rivers, and draws lots of tourists every year.

ctx.s: 她出生在南方一个{山清水秀}的小村子。
ctx.en: She was born in a small village in the south surrounded by green hills and clear water.

ctx.s: “退休以后想住哪儿？”“找个{山清水秀}的地方，种种菜，钓钓鱼。”
ctx.en: "Where do you want to live after you retire?" "Somewhere with green hills and clear rivers, where I can grow vegetables and go fishing."

ctx.s: 这里以前到处是工厂，现在治理好了，又变得{山清水秀}。
ctx.en: There used to be factories everywhere here; now it's been cleaned up and the hills and rivers are lovely again.

ctx.s: 照片上的小镇{山清水秀}，像一幅画。
ctx.en: The town in the photo, with its green hills and clear water, looks like a painting.

ctx.s: 心情不好的时候，去{山清水秀}的地方走走，会好很多。
ctx.en: When you're feeling down, a walk somewhere with green hills and clear water makes you feel much better.

bad.s: 这个城市高楼很多，真是{山清水秀}。
bad.why: It praises natural hills and rivers, not a cityscape of tall buildings.

bad.s: 她长得{山清水秀}，很多人追她。
bad.why: It describes landscape only; for a person's delicate good looks say méi qīng mù xiù or qīng xiù.

mean: packed so tight nothing can get through
lit: not even water could seep through

use.how: Usually a complement after 挤得, 堵得, 围得 (围了个水泄不通), about crowds, traffic or a cordon blocking a place.

near.diff: 滴水不漏 praises a plan or speech with no flaw; 水泄不通 describes a place physically jammed by people, cars or a cordon.

cue: Thousands of fans surround the hotel entrance so tightly that nobody can get in or out.

ctx.s: 演唱会门口挤得{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: The entrance to the concert was packed solid.

ctx.s: 下班高峰，这条路堵得{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: At rush hour this road is completely jammed.

ctx.s: “你怎么迟到了？”“商场在打折，电梯口被围得{水泄不通}。”
ctx.en: "Why are you late?" "The mall's having a sale, and the lifts were completely mobbed."

ctx.s: 明星一出机场，就被粉丝围了个{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: The moment the star walked out of the airport, fans packed in around him so tight no one could move.

ctx.s: 春节前的火车站{水泄不通}，买票要排很久。
ctx.en: Before Spring Festival the railway station is jam-packed, and you queue for ages to buy a ticket.

ctx.s: 警察把事故现场围得{水泄不通}，谁也进不去。
ctx.en: The police sealed off the accident scene completely; nobody could get in.

bad.s: 这个杯子{水泄不通}，一滴水都不漏。
bad.why: It is about crowds, traffic or a cordon blocking a place, not about objects that don't leak.

bad.s: 他的计划{水泄不通}，没有一点漏洞。
bad.why: For a flawless plan or argument use dī shuǐ bù lòu or tiān yī wú fèng; this idiom means a place is physically packed.

mean: to make a tense or angry situation even worse
lit: to pour oil onto a fire

use.how: Predicate, or after 是, 等于, 无异于: 你这么说是火上浇油. Criticises words or actions that inflame someone's anger or a conflict.

near.diff: 雪上加霜 is one misfortune piled on another; 火上浇油 is making anger or a conflict flare up further.

cue: Your manager is already furious about the delay, and a colleague picks that moment to point out three more mistakes.

ctx.s: 他已经很生气了，你别再{火上浇油}了。
ctx.en: He's already really angry; don't make it worse.

ctx.s: 妈妈正在骂弟弟，姐姐在旁边说风凉话，简直是{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: Mum was scolding my little brother, and my sister stood there making snide remarks, which only made things worse.

ctx.s: 两家公司本来就有矛盾，这篇报道更是{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: The two companies were already at odds, and this report only inflamed things further.

ctx.s: “我要不要现在去跟老板解释？”“现在去只会{火上浇油}，等他冷静了再说。”
ctx.en: "Should I go and explain to the boss now?" "Going now will only make him angrier; wait until he's calmed down."

ctx.s: 球迷本来就不满，裁判的错判无异于{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: The fans were already unhappy, and the referee's bad call was like pouring oil on the fire.

ctx.s: 吵架的时候翻旧账，等于{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: Dragging up old grievances in the middle of a fight just adds fuel to the fire.

bad.s: 他刚丢了工作，又生了病，真是{火上浇油}。
bad.en: (meant: one misfortune on top of another)
bad.why: That is xuě shàng jiā shuāng. This idiom is about making anger or a conflict flare up, not bad luck piling up.

bad.s: 大家干得正起劲，老板又发了奖金，真是{火上浇油}。
bad.en: (meant: the bonus made a good thing even better)
bad.why: It is always negative. For adding something good to what is already good, use jǐn shàng tiān huā.

lit: in keeping with feeling and in keeping with reason

use.how: Predicate or attributive judging a request, explanation, decision or arrangement: 这个要求合情合理 / 合情合理的安排.

near.diff: 理所当然 says something naturally follows and needs no argument; 合情合理 judges it fair, both humanly and logically.

cue: A worker asks for overtime pay after staying late all week. Everyone agrees the request is fair, both legally and humanly.

ctx.s: 他的要求{合情合理}，我们应该答应。
ctx.en: His request is fair and reasonable; we should agree to it.

ctx.s: 加班就给加班费，这是{合情合理}的事。
ctx.en: If you work overtime, you get overtime pay; that's only fair.

ctx.s: “我请三天假，你觉得过分吗？”“家里有急事，请假{合情合理}。”
ctx.en: "Do you think asking for three days off is too much?" "You've got a family emergency; it's perfectly reasonable."

ctx.s: 法官的判决{合情合理}，双方都接受了。
ctx.en: The judge's ruling was fair and reasonable, and both sides accepted it.

ctx.s: 这个解释听起来{合情合理}，可我总觉得哪里不对。
ctx.en: The explanation sounds perfectly reasonable, but I still feel something's off.

ctx.s: 房东涨了一点房租，考虑到物价，也算{合情合理}。
ctx.en: The landlord raised the rent a little, which, given prices, is fair enough.

bad.s: 他是个{合情合理}的人，从不乱发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a reasonable, understanding person)
bad.why: It judges a request, explanation or decision, not a person's character; for a sensible, understanding person say tōng qíng dá lǐ.

bad.s: 这道数学题的答案{合情合理}。
bad.en: (meant: the answer to this maths problem is correct)
bad.why: It is about fairness in human affairs, not correctness; a maths answer is simply right or wrong.
